editorNote: Open weights, a stable Go package and a vendor's odd network sighting: three kinds of announcement, one rule of thumb. The numbers are mostly the authors' own.

stories.headline: Moonshot releases Kimi K3.1 Pro weights: 2.8T parameters, 104B active
stories.summary: The model card describes an open-weight, natively multimodal agentic mixture-of-experts model with a 1M-token context window, under a custom licence. Moonshot's own benchmarks include 94.2 on GPQA-Diamond.
stories.whyItMatters: A second very large open-weight model is available to download, but the licence is not a standard open-source one and the scores are vendor-reported.

stories.headline: Go 1.27 makes encoding/json/v2 generally available
stories.summary: The Go blog says the new JSON packages are stable, with stricter defaults (invalid UTF-8 and duplicate names are errors) and unmarshaling up to 10x faster; v1 stays supported and now runs on top of v2.
stories.whyItMatters: Teams can migrate gradually, with options to keep v1 behaviours, rather than rewriting JSON handling at once.

sourceLinks.title: A new Go API for JSON (Go Blog)

stories.headline: Ricursive's Ripple-65B Preview claims open-weight agentic-coding lead
stories.summary: The 65B dense model scores 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1 by the company's account, and is on Hugging Face, Together AI, GMI Cloud and OpenRouter. The company says training cost about $32M; the page states no licence.
stories.whyItMatters: A smaller open model claiming to top larger ones is notable, but every figure here, including cost, is the vendor's own.

stories.headline: Vendor reports residential-proxy exits on the Executive Office of the President's network
stories.summary: Layer3 Intel says it saw 236 proxy exits through AS2650 over 30 days, across 6 addresses. It calls this suggestive of a person's infected device, but says its data shows only the exits.
stories.whyItMatters: Exit traffic is not proof of a breach, and the claims come from a vendor selling detection and publishing no raw data.

sourceLinks.title: Residential proxies detected on White House network (Layer3 Intel)
